dedupe_keys.name: un humanitarian response depot unhrd hub network and storage capacities

description: This page describes the network of humanitarian supply hubs run by the UN Humanitarian Response Depot (UNHRD), managed by the World Food Programme, which offers free storage, prepositioned relief items and technical support to humanitarian partners. It lists the five hubs, in Accra, Brindisi, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur and Panama City, with the year each started, its host government and site, and its facilities: covered and open storage area, temperature-controlled space, cold rooms and freezers, office space and training centres. For example, Dubai has 11,520 square metres of covered space and 3,360 square metres of temperature-controlled space, and Brindisi 8,500 square metres of covered space. Coverage is global, one entry per hub. The information is free to read on the web, with no download and no stated licence. Caveats: the page gives capacities, not current stock levels or throughput, and it may lag changes to the network. Simulation uses: locations and capacities of prepositioning depots for emergency relief supply chain and response models. Related records: the UNHRD stock taskforce study (case_study-unhrd-stock-taskforce-prepositioning-ceilings) analyses prepositioning in this network, and the WFP Logistics Database (data-wfp-logistics-database-sdi-t) covers wider logistics infrastructure.
